source.text: Πέτρος ἀπόστολος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐκλεκτοῖς παρεπιδήμοις διασπορᾶς Πόντου, Γαλατίας, Καππαδοκίας, Ἀσίας, καὶ Βιθυνίας, κατὰ πρόγνωσιν θεοῦ πατρός, ἐν ἁγιασμῷ πνεύματος, εἰς ὑπακοὴν καὶ ῥαντισμὸν αἵματος Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ· χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη πληθυνθείη.

records.literal_gloss: Peter, apostle of Jesus Christ, to [the] chosen sojourners of [the] dispersion of Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia, \v 2 according to foreknowledge of God Father, in sanctification of [the] Spirit, unto obedience and sprinkling of [the] blood of Jesus Christ: grace to you and peace may it be multiplied.

en.L: Peter, an apostle of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, to [the] chosen [ones] living as foreigners in [the] dispersion of Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia, \v 2 according to [the] foreknowledge of God [the] Father, by [the] setting apart of [the] Spirit, for obedience and sprinkling of [the] blood of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}: may grace to you and peace be multiplied.
en.B: From Peter, an apostle of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, to those God has chosen who live as foreigners, scattered through Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia. \v 2 God the Father chose you as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} knew beforehand, and the Spirit set you apart, so that you would obey Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} and be sprinkled with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} blood. May grace and peace be yours in ever greater measure.
en.R: This letter is from Peter, an apostle sent out by Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. I am writing to God's chosen people, who are living as foreigners, scattered through the provinces of Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia. \v 2 God the Father knew you and chose you long ago. The Spirit has set you apart as God's holy people, so that you would obey Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} and be made clean by the sprinkling of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} blood. May God give you more and more grace and peace.

decisions.choice: people chosen by God who live as foreigners, scattered away from home
alternatives: Jewish exiles of the dispersion in the narrow sense
refugees or displaced migrants in a purely social sense
decisions.reason: παρεπιδήμοις are people staying for a time in a place that is not their home; διασπορᾶς is the word for the scattering of the Jewish people among the nations. The letter applies both to the church as a whole: its readers once lived an empty way of life inherited from their ancestors (1:18) and did not know God (1:14), so most were probably not Jews by birth. They are foreigners because their true home and inheritance are with God (1:4, 17; 2:11). Whether some were also foreigners in a legal or social sense cannot be settled from the letter.

decisions.choice: Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, Bithynia: Roman regions of Asia Minor, in present-day Turkey
decisions.reason: Together they cover most of Asia Minor north and west of the Taurus mountains. Pontus and Bithynia were joined as one Roman province, but the letter names them separately, perhaps in the order a messenger carrying the letter would travel, beginning and ending near the Black Sea coast.

decisions.choice: the three phrases of verse 2 describe how the readers were chosen: by the Father's foreknowledge, through the Spirit's setting apart, for obedience and sprinkling with Christ's blood
alternatives: they describe Peter's being an apostle
decisions.reason: The phrases follow ἐκλεκτοῖς and fit it best: being chosen has its source in the Father, its means in the Spirit, and its goal in Jesus Christ. Father, Spirit and Jesus Christ are all named in one sentence. πρόγνωσιν is more than knowing facts in advance; it is God's knowing and choosing beforehand, as the same word is used of Christ in 1:20.

decisions.choice: obedience and sprinkling with blood recall the making of the covenant at Sinai
alternatives: sprinkling as a picture of cleansing only
decisions.reason: In Exodus 24:3-8 the people promise to obey everything the LORD has said, and Moses sprinkles them with the blood of the covenant. Peter puts the same two things together for the church: obedience, and being sprinkled with the blood of Jesus Christ, which brings them into the covenant and makes them clean (compare Hebrews 9:19-22; 12:24).

decisions.choice: "of Jesus Christ" goes with "blood"; obedience is obedience to Jesus Christ
alternatives: "of Jesus Christ" with both nouns: "the obedience of Jesus Christ" (his own obedience) and his blood
decisions.reason: The two nouns share one phrase, and Jesus Christ is certainly the one whose blood is sprinkled. Whether the readers' obedience or Christ's own obedience is meant is less clear, but the letter elsewhere speaks of the readers' obedience (1:14, 22), and the Sinai pattern of verse 2 is the people obeying.

decisions.choice: the Spirit's work of setting people apart for God
alternatives: a holiness of the human spirit
decisions.reason: ἁγιασμῷ is the act of making holy, setting apart for God. πνεύματος is God's Spirit, named between the Father and Jesus Christ; the Spirit is the one who does the setting apart.

decisions.choice: a wish or prayer: may grace and peace be multiplied to you
decisions.reason: πληθυνθείη is in the form Greek uses for wishes. The same greeting opens 2 Peter (2 Peter 1:2) and is found in Daniel's Greek (Daniel 4:1).

decisions.choice: Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R); {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} for Christ
decisions.reason: Title and pronoun settings.

decisions.choice: living as foreigners
decisions.reason: "Exiles" suggests people forced out of their own country, which the Greek does not say; "sojourners" is no longer everyday English. "Living as foreigners" says what the word means: people who live in a place that is not their home.

decisions.choice: knew you and chose you long ago; made you his own holy people; made clean by the sprinkling
alternatives: according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, in the sanctification of the Spirit, for the sprinkling of blood
decisions.reason: Readable explains foreknowledge, setting apart and sprinkling in plain words. "Made clean" draws on what sprinkling with blood did in the Old Testament (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: May grace and peace be yours in ever greater measure (B); May God give you more and more grace and peace (R)
alternatives: Grace and peace be multiplied to you
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the wish in the passive; Readable names God as the giver, as the opening greetings of Colossians and Philippians do at Readable.

source.text: Εὐλογητὸς ὁ θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ τοῦ κυρίου ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὁ κατὰ τὸ πολὺ αὐτοῦ ἔλεος ἀναγεννήσας ἡμᾶς εἰς ἐλπίδα ζῶσαν δι’ ἀναστάσεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐκ νεκρῶν, εἰς κληρονομίαν ἄφθαρτον καὶ ἀμίαντον καὶ ἀμάραντον, τετηρημένην ἐν οὐρανοῖς εἰς ὑμᾶς τοὺς ἐν δυνάμει θεοῦ φρουρουμένους διὰ πίστεως εἰς σωτηρίαν ἑτοίμην ἀποκαλυφθῆναι ἐν καιρῷ ἐσχάτῳ.

records.literal_gloss: Blessed [be] the God and Father of the Lord of us Jesus Christ, the [one] according to the much of him mercy having begotten again us into hope living through resurrection of Jesus Christ out of dead [ones], \v 4 into inheritance imperishable and undefiled and unfading, having been kept in heavens for you, \v 5 the [ones] in power of God being guarded through faith for salvation ready to be revealed in time last.

en.L: Blessed [be] the God and Father of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, who according to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great mercy begot us again into a living hope through [the] resurrection of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} out of [the] dead, \v 4 into an inheritance imperishable and unstained and unwithering, kept in [the] heavens for you, \v 5 who in [the] power of God are kept under guard through faith for a salvation ready to be revealed in [the] last time.
en.B: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}! Out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great mercy {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given us a new birth. Through the resurrection of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} from the dead {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has brought us into a hope that is alive, \v 4 and into an inheritance that can never decay, never be stained, and never wither. That inheritance is kept safe in heaven for you, \v 5 and God's power is keeping you under guard through faith until the salvation that stands ready to be revealed at the last time.
en.R: Praise the God and Father of our Lord Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}! God is so full of mercy that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has given us a new birth. He did this by raising Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} from the dead, and so we now have a hope that is alive. \v 4 God is keeping a gift for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} children, and it can never be ruined, spoiled, or faded. It is kept safe for you in heaven. \v 5 And God's power is keeping you safe through your faith, until the salvation that is ready and waiting is shown at the end of time.

decisions.choice: a declaration of praise: God is blessed, that is, worthy of praise
alternatives: a wish that God would be blessed or made happy
decisions.reason: This is the form of Jewish blessings of God, "Blessed be the LORD" (Psalm 72:18; compare 2 Corinthians 1:3; Ephesians 1:3). There is no verb in the Greek; the sentence praises God for what follows.

decisions.choice: caused to be born a second time, given new life by God as Father
decisions.reason: ἀναγεννήσας is "beget again": God, just called "Father", gives his people a new birth. The same verb returns in 1:23, where the seed of this birth is God's word.

decisions.choice: the new birth comes through Jesus' resurrection, and it brings a hope that is alive
alternatives: the resurrection explains only why the hope is living
decisions.reason: The phrase about the resurrection can go with "begot us again" or with "living hope". Either way the resurrection is the source: because Jesus Christ lives, the hope he gives is alive and sure, not an empty wish.

decisions.choice: inheritance: a share kept for God's children, like the land promised to Israel but beyond any loss
decisions.reason: In the Old Testament Israel's inheritance was the land (Numbers 26:52-56; Deuteronomy 4:21). That land could be ruined, defiled and lost (Jeremiah 2:7). The three words of verse 4 each begin with a Greek "not": this inheritance cannot perish, be stained or wither. It is kept, and the perfect participle τετηρημένην says it is already being held safe in heaven.

decisions.choice: the readers are continually guarded by God's power, and faith is the means by which that protection reaches them
decisions.reason: φρουρουμένους is a military word for a garrison guarding a town, and it is present: the guarding goes on now. God's power does the guarding; "through faith" says how the readers share in it.

decisions.choice: salvation in its full and final form, made known at the end, when Jesus Christ is revealed
decisions.reason: Salvation is already prepared and waiting (ἑτοίμην); what remains is for it to be revealed. "The last time" is the time of Christ's revealing (1:7, 13), when what is hidden now is seen.

decisions.choice: Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L), Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R); {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} for God
decisions.reason: Title and pronoun settings.

decisions.choice: begot us again (L); has given us a new birth (B, R)
alternatives: caused us to be born again
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the image of a father begetting, which follows from "God and Father". Balanced and Readable use the plain idea of a new birth.

decisions.choice: He did this by raising Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} from the dead; a gift for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} children
alternatives: through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead; an inheritance
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who raised Jesus (as 1:21 does) and explains "inheritance" as what a father keeps for his children.

decisions.choice: Praise
decisions.reason: "Blessed be God" is church language; Readable says what it means.

source.text: ἐν ᾧ ἀγαλλιᾶσθε, ὀλίγον ἄρτι εἰ δέον λυπηθέντες ἐν ποικίλοις πειρασμοῖς, ἵνα τὸ δοκίμιον ὑμῶν τῆς πίστεως πολυτιμότερον χρυσίου τοῦ ἀπολλυμένου διὰ πυρὸς δὲ δοκιμαζομένου εὑρεθῇ εἰς ἔπαινον καὶ δόξαν καὶ τιμὴν ἐν ἀποκαλύψει Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: In which you rejoice greatly, a little now if necessary having been grieved in various trials, \v 7 so that the tested [genuineness] of you of the faith, more precious than gold the [gold] perishing but through fire being tested, may be found unto praise and glory and honor in [the] revealing of Jesus Christ.

en.L: In this you are overjoyed, though for a little while now, if it has to be, you have been grieved by trials of many kinds, \v 7 so that the tested worth of your faith, more precious than gold, which perishes though proved by fire, may be found to [bring] praise and glory and honor at [the] revealing of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: This is why you are overjoyed, even though for a little while now, if it must be so, you have been distressed by trials of many kinds. \v 7 They come so that your faith, once tested and shown to be genuine, may be found to bring praise and glory and honor at the time Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is revealed. Faith like that is worth far more than gold, and gold perishes, even though it too is tested by fire.
en.R: This gives you great joy, even though for a short time you may have to be sad because of many kinds of troubles. \v 7 These troubles test your faith and show that it is real. Gold is tested in fire, and even gold does not last forever. But your faith is worth much more than gold. When it has been tested and proved true, it will lead to praise and glory and honor when Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is revealed.

decisions.choice: "in this": the readers rejoice in all that verses 3-5 have said God has done and is keeping for them
alternatives: "in which [last time]": you will rejoice when the last time comes
decisions.reason: ἐν ᾧ can refer to the last word of verse 5, "time", to God, or to the whole of verses 3-5. The joy is present and it exists alongside present grief, so the broad reference fits best; but the other readings are possible.

decisions.choice: a statement, "you rejoice", describing their present joy
alternatives: a present with future meaning, "you will rejoice"
decisions.reason: ἀγαλλιᾶσθε has the same form for statement and command. The same verb in 1:8 is clearly a statement about what the readers already do, and the joy here is set beside grief they have actually felt, so it is a statement here too.

decisions.choice: the grief is real but short, and comes only as God allows it
decisions.reason: λυπηθέντες is a concession: they rejoice even though they have been grieved. "For a little while" sets the present trouble against the inheritance that does not fade. εἰ δέον, "if it must be", treats suffering as something that comes only when it is God's will (compare 3:17; 4:19).

decisions.choice: the genuineness of faith that has been proved by testing
decisions.reason: δοκίμιον can mean a test or what a test shows. Here it is said to be more precious than gold and to end in praise, which fits the tested and proven quality better than the testing process.

decisions.choice: faith is tested the way gold is tested in the fire, but it is worth more than gold
decisions.reason: The refiner's fire is an Old Testament picture of God testing his people (Psalm 66:10; Proverbs 17:3; Zechariah 13:9). Peter argues from the lesser to the greater: if people test gold, which perishes in the end, faith that will last is worth far more.

decisions.choice: the praise, glory and honor are given to the believers whose faith proved true, at Christ's revealing
alternatives: the praise and glory are given to God, or to Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: The praise is the result of the tested faith being "found". Elsewhere in the New Testament God gives praise and glory to those who have been faithful (Romans 2:7, 29; 1 Corinthians 4:5; 1 Peter 5:4), and that fits here. Since all such honor comes from God, his glory is not excluded.

decisions.choice: revealing: the day Jesus Christ, now unseen, is openly shown when he returns
decisions.reason: ἀποκαλύψει looks to the end, as in 1:13 and 4:13. The readers do not see Jesus now (1:8); at his revealing he will be seen.

decisions.choice: Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L), Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: are overjoyed
decisions.reason: ἀγαλλιᾶσθε is a strong word for exultant joy; "overjoyed" carries that strength. The same choice is made in 1:8.

decisions.choice: the comparison with gold moved to a sentence of its own
alternatives: the comparison kept in the middle of the sentence, as in Literal
decisions.reason: In Greek the comparison with gold interrupts the sentence. Balanced and Readable give it its own sentence so that the main line, faith tested and found to bring praise, can be followed.

source.text: ὃν οὐκ ἰδόντες ἀγαπᾶτε, εἰς ὃν ἄρτι μὴ ὁρῶντες πιστεύοντες δὲ ἀγαλλιᾶσθε χαρᾷ ἀνεκλαλήτῳ καὶ δεδοξασμένῃ, κομιζόμενοι τὸ τέλος τῆς πίστεως ὑμῶν σωτηρίαν ψυχῶν.

records.literal_gloss: whom not having seen you love, in whom now not seeing but believing you rejoice greatly with joy inexpressible and glorified, \v 9 receiving the end of the faith of you, salvation of souls.

en.L: Whom, not having seen [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], you love; in whom, though not seeing [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] now but believing, you are overjoyed with joy inexpressible and glorified, \v 9 receiving the goal of your faith, [the] salvation of souls.
en.B: You have never seen {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, yet you love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. You do not see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} even now, but you believe in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and you are overjoyed with a joy that words cannot express, a joy already filled with glory, \v 9 because you are receiving what your faith aims at: the salvation of your souls.
en.R: You have never seen Jesus, but you love {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. You cannot see {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} now, but you believe in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. And so you are filled with a joy too great for words, a joy full of glory. \v 9 For you are receiving what your faith was looking forward to: God saves you, all that you are.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "not having seen"
alternatives: "not knowing" (a different Greek word of similar spelling)
decisions.reason: Early and important manuscripts read ἰδόντες, "having seen". Many later manuscripts have a word meaning "knowing", which would say that the readers love one they do not know. "Seen" fits the contrast with "not seeing now" in the next clause. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: statements of what the readers do now: they love Jesus and rejoice
decisions.reason: Both verbs have forms that could be commands, but the sentence describes the readers' present faith and joy, as 1:6 does.

decisions.choice: glorified: joy already touched by the glory of the age to come
alternatives: glorious in the general sense of splendid
decisions.reason: δεδοξασμένῃ is a perfect passive participle of "glorify": the joy has been given glory. Peter has just spoken of glory at Christ's revealing (1:7); the readers' joy now already shares in it.

decisions.choice: the readers are already receiving their salvation, which will be complete at the end
alternatives: they will receive it only at the end
decisions.reason: κομιζόμενοι is present: they are receiving it now. Verse 5 says salvation will be revealed in the last time; the two belong together, as present and future of the same salvation.

decisions.choice: end: the goal and result toward which faith is directed
alternatives: the end in time, when faith stops
decisions.reason: τέλος can mean an end in time or a goal. Here what faith reaches is salvation, so it is the goal faith aims at.

decisions.choice: souls: the whole person, the self that lives, not an immaterial part as opposed to the body
alternatives: the soul in distinction from the body
decisions.reason: In the Greek Bible ψυχῶν often means persons or lives (Genesis 46:27; Acts 2:41), and 1 Peter uses it that way (3:20, "eight souls"). The whole person is saved, including the body raised at the end (1:3).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}
decisions.reason: Pronoun setting: Jesus Christ is meant.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: The relative pronoun points back to Jesus Christ at the end of verse 7. Readable starts a new sentence and names him.

decisions.choice: a joy that words cannot express (B); too great for words (R)
decisions.reason: ἀνεκλαλήτῳ means what cannot be spoken out; the plain phrase says so without a rare word.

decisions.choice: God saves you, all that you are
decisions.reason: Readable says that the whole person is saved, following meaning decision m6, and names God as the one who saves.

source.text: Περὶ ἧς σωτηρίας ἐξεζήτησαν καὶ ἐξηραύνησαν προφῆται οἱ περὶ τῆς εἰς ὑμᾶς χάριτος προφητεύσαντες, ἐραυνῶντες εἰς τίνα ἢ ποῖον καιρὸν ἐδήλου τὸ ἐν αὐτοῖς πνεῦμα Χριστοῦ προμαρτυρόμενον τὰ εἰς Χριστὸν παθήματα καὶ τὰς μετὰ ταῦτα δόξας·

records.literal_gloss: Concerning which salvation sought out and searched out [the] prophets, the [ones] concerning the toward you grace having prophesied, \v 11 searching into what or what sort of time was making clear the in them Spirit of Christ, testifying beforehand the toward Christ sufferings and the after these glories.

en.L: Concerning this salvation prophets sought and searched carefully, those who prophesied about the grace [meant] for you, \v 11 searching into what time or what kind of time the Spirit of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} in them was making clear, testifying beforehand to the sufferings [destined] for {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} and the glories after these.
en.B: This salvation is what the prophets looked into, searching it out with great care, when they prophesied about the grace God meant for you. \v 11 They tried to learn what time, and what sort of time, was being shown to them by the Spirit of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} who was in them, as the Spirit told beforehand of the sufferings in store for {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} and the glories to come after them.
en.R: Long ago the prophets spoke about the grace God was going to give you. They studied hard and searched carefully to understand this salvation. \v 11 The Spirit of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} was in them, and told them ahead of time that {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} would suffer and then receive glory. So they tried to find out when this would happen and what that time would be like.

decisions.choice: the prophets of the Old Testament
decisions.reason: They prophesied about grace that was to come to the readers and searched for the time it would happen, so they lived before it. Their message was not for themselves but for later readers (1:12).

decisions.choice: "what time or what kind of time": both words ask about the time
alternatives: "what person or what time": who the Messiah would be, and when he would come
decisions.reason: τίνα can stand alone as "whom" or go with καιρὸν as "what time". Peter's next sentence says the prophets learned that the things were for a later generation, an answer about time, and the phrase reads naturally as one question asked two ways. The other reading is possible and well supported.

decisions.choice: the Spirit of Christ was already at work in the prophets
alternatives: a spirit that points toward the Messiah, not the Spirit of God himself
decisions.reason: Peter calls the Spirit who spoke through the prophets "the Spirit of Christ", the same Holy Spirit sent from heaven in 1:12. The prophets' words about the Messiah came from the Messiah's own Spirit (compare 2 Peter 1:21).

decisions.choice: the sufferings destined for the Messiah, that he himself would undergo
alternatives: the sufferings of Christians for Christ's sake
decisions.reason: εἰς Χριστὸν is literally "toward Christ". The Spirit testified ahead of time about what would happen to the Messiah, as in Isaiah 53, and the letter returns to Christ's own sufferings and glory often (2:21-24; 3:18-22; 4:13; 5:1).

decisions.choice: glories, plural: the glorious events that followed the sufferings, such as resurrection, ascension and exaltation
decisions.reason: δόξας is plural. 3:18-22 traces the path: put to death, made alive, gone into heaven, with angels and powers subject to him.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L), {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: the glories (L, B); receive glory (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the plural of the key term glory, which points to more than one glorious event. Readable says it with the verb "receive glory".

decisions.choice: the Spirit (repeated); no "it" for the Spirit
decisions.reason: English would need a pronoun for the Spirit who testified. The Spirit is never "it" in this translation, so Balanced repeats "the Spirit" and Literal uses a participle.

decisions.choice: the prophets' prophecy put first, then their searching
alternatives: concerning this salvation the prophets searched
decisions.reason: Readable tells the events in the order they happened.

source.text: οἷς ἀπεκαλύφθη ὅτι οὐχ ἑαυτοῖς ὑμῖν δὲ διηκόνουν αὐτά, ἃ νῦν ἀνηγγέλη ὑμῖν διὰ τῶν εὐαγγελισαμένων ὑμᾶς πνεύματι ἁγίῳ ἀποσταλέντι ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ, εἰς ἃ ἐπιθυμοῦσιν ἄγγελοι παρακύψαι.

records.literal_gloss: to whom it was revealed that not to themselves but to you they were serving them, which now were announced to you through the [ones] having proclaimed good news [to] you by [the] Spirit Holy sent from heaven, into which long angels to stoop to look.

en.L: To them it was revealed that it was not for themselves but for you that they were ministering these [things], which now have been reported to you through those who proclaimed the good news to you by [the] Holy Spirit sent from heaven, [things] into which angels desire to bend down and look.
en.B: God showed the prophets that what they spoke of was not for their own benefit; they were serving you. Those same things have now been reported to you by the people who brought you the good news through the Holy Spirit, who was sent from heaven. Even angels long to bend down and look into these things.
en.R: God showed the prophets that their message was not for themselves but for you. Now this message has been told to you by the people who brought you the good news. They spoke by the power of the Holy Spirit, whom God sent from heaven. Even the angels long to look closely into these things.

decisions.choice: it was God who revealed it to the prophets
decisions.reason: οἷς points back to the prophets of verse 10. ἀπεκαλύφθη is passive, the usual way of speaking of what God does without naming him.

decisions.choice: the prophets served later believers by speaking of things that have now been announced in the gospel
decisions.reason: διηκόνουν is the verb of serving or ministering. αὐτά and ἃ refer to the sufferings and glories of the Messiah (1:11): the prophets foretold them, and the evangelists have now announced them as fulfilled.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "for you", and "by the Holy Spirit" without the preposition "in"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "for us" instead of "for you"; the two Greek words differ by one letter and were often confused. Some manuscripts add "in" before "Holy Spirit", which does not change the meaning. Reviewers must check both against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Holy Spirit, sent from heaven, gave power to those who preached the gospel
decisions.reason: The Spirit who spoke beforehand in the prophets (1:11) is the same Spirit sent from heaven, as at Pentecost (Acts 2:1-4, 33), who empowered the preaching the readers heard.

decisions.choice: angels long to bend down and look closely: they eagerly want to see these things
alternatives: angels once wanted to look, but now see fully
decisions.reason: παρακύψαι is to stoop or bend over to look, as the disciples stooped to look into the empty tomb (John 20:5, 11). ἐπιθυμοῦσιν is present: the angels go on longing. Salvation is a privilege the readers enjoy that even angels look into from outside.

decisions.choice: God showed the prophets
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God and the prophets, following meaning decision m1.

decisions.choice: They spoke by the power of the Holy Spirit, whom God sent
alternatives: by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven
decisions.reason: Readable says how the Spirit was involved (with power) and who sent him.

decisions.choice: proclaimed the good news (L); brought you the good news (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek is the verb "announce good news". Gospel, the key term, translates the related noun; for the verb all levels say "good news", as 1:25 does.

source.text: Διὸ ἀναζωσάμενοι τὰς ὀσφύας τῆς διανοίας ὑμῶν, νήφοντες τελείως, ἐλπίσατε ἐπὶ τὴν φερομένην ὑμῖν χάριν ἐν ἀποκαλύψει Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore having girded up the loins of the mind of you, being sober, completely hope upon the being brought to you grace in [the] revealing of Jesus Christ.

en.L: Therefore, having girded up the loins of your mind, staying sober, hope wholly on the grace being carried to you at [the] revealing of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: So brace your minds for action and stay clear-headed. Put your hope entirely on the grace that is coming to you when Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is revealed.
en.R: So get your minds ready to act, and think clearly. Put all your hope in the grace God will give you when Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is revealed.

decisions.choice: get your minds ready for action
decisions.reason: To gird up one's loins was to tuck a long robe into the belt so as to work, run or travel. Israel ate the Passover dressed this way, ready to leave Egypt (Exodus 12:11; compare Luke 12:35). Peter applies the picture to the mind.

decisions.choice: sober: clear-headed and self-controlled
alternatives: not drunk, in a literal sense only
decisions.reason: νήφοντες is literally being sober. Peter uses the word for alert self-control in 4:7 and 5:8.

decisions.choice: "completely" goes with "hope": hope fully
alternatives: "completely" goes with "being sober": be fully sober
decisions.reason: τελείως stands between the two verbs. Most often an adverb like this follows the word it describes, which would favor "fully sober"; but the main command is "hope", and placing all hope on the coming grace makes a strong sense. The evidence is close to even.

decisions.choice: a command to hope, with the two participles telling how
decisions.reason: ἐλπίσατε is the only command; the participles take on its force ("gird up... be sober... hope").

decisions.choice: the grace is already on its way and will arrive at Christ's revealing
alternatives: the grace given now, during the present life
decisions.reason: φερομένην is present, "being brought", but it is tied to the revealing of Jesus Christ. Grace here is the full gift God will give at the end.

decisions.choice: Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L), Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: brace your minds for action (B); get your minds ready to act (R)
alternatives: gird up the loins of your mind
decisions.reason: Readers today do not wear robes tied with a belt; Balanced and Readable say what the picture means (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the image.

decisions.choice: the grace God will give you
alternatives: the grace being brought to you
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the giver of grace.

source.text: ὡς τέκνα ὑπακοῆς, μὴ συσχηματιζόμενοι ταῖς πρότερον ἐν τῇ ἀγνοίᾳ ὑμῶν ἐπιθυμίαις, ἀλλὰ κατὰ τὸν καλέσαντα ὑμᾶς ἅγιον καὶ αὐτοὶ ἅγιοι ἐν πάσῃ ἀναστροφῇ γενήθητε, διότι γέγραπται ὅτι Ἅγιοι ἔσεσθε, ὅτι ἐγὼ ἅγιος.

records.literal_gloss: as children of obedience, not conforming yourselves to the formerly in the ignorance of you desires, \v 15 but according to the [one] having called you holy also yourselves holy in all conduct become, \v 16 because it has been written: Holy you will be, because I holy.

en.L: As children of obedience, not conforming yourselves to the desires [you had] formerly in your ignorance, \v 15 but just as the one who called you [is] holy, you yourselves also become holy in all [your] conduct, \v 16 because it is written, "You will be holy, because I [am] holy."
en.B: Live as children who obey. Do not let yourselves be shaped by the desires you used to follow back when you did not know any better. \v 15 Instead, be holy yourselves in all your conduct, just as the one who called you is holy, \v 16 because it is written, "You are to be holy, because I am holy."
en.R: Be like children who obey. Do not let your lives be shaped by the desires you followed before, when you did not know God. \v 15 God, who called you, is holy. So you must be holy in everything you do. \v 16 For the Scriptures say, "You must be holy, because I am holy."

decisions.choice: obedient children
decisions.reason: "Children of" followed by a quality is a Hebrew way of describing someone by that quality (compare Ephesians 2:2-3, "children of wrath"). The readers are children marked by obeying God, their Father (1:17).

decisions.choice: the ignorance of their former life, before they knew God
decisions.reason: ἀγνοίᾳ describes the time before they came to know God, as with the nations in Acts 17:30. With 1:18 and 4:3-4, it suggests that most readers had not been Jews.

decisions.choice: a call to a whole new way of life: stop being shaped by old desires, and become holy in everything
decisions.reason: συσχηματιζόμενοι is to take the shape of something (as in Romans 12:2). γενήθητε is a command: "become" or "be" holy, in every part of how they live (ἀναστροφῇ, a favorite word of this letter: 1:17, 18; 2:12; 3:1-2, 16).

decisions.choice: holy: set apart to belong to God, and so different in character and conduct
decisions.reason: God is holy, and those he calls are to share his holiness. In Leviticus this meant both belonging to God and living differently from the surrounding nations; Peter means both.

decisions.choice: the quotation is from Leviticus
decisions.reason: The words "You will be holy, because I am holy" occur in Leviticus 11:44-45; 19:2; 20:7, 26. In Leviticus 19:2 the LORD tells Moses to say this to all Israel; in 11:44-45 it comes after the LORD reminds them he brought them out of Egypt. Peter applies Israel's calling to the church.

decisions.choice: a future used as a command: you are to be holy
alternatives: a promise: you will become holy
decisions.reason: In the commands of the law the future often has the force of an imperative ("you shall").

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "you will be holy, because I holy" without "am"
alternatives: "become holy" in place of "you will be holy"
"I am holy" with the verb written out
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read a command form "become" in place of "you will be", and many add the word for "am". Neither changes the meaning; where "am" is not written, it is understood. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: it is written
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the familiar formula for quoting Scripture; it still reads as plain English.

decisions.choice: God, who called you; For the Scriptures say
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who called, and says where the words are written.

decisions.choice: Live as children who obey (B); Be like children who obey (R)
decisions.reason: The phrase goes with the commands that follow; Balanced and Readable give it a verb so it can stand as an English sentence.

source.text: Καὶ εἰ πατέρα ἐπικαλεῖσθε τὸν ἀπροσωπολήμπτως κρίνοντα κατὰ τὸ ἑκάστου ἔργον, ἐν φόβῳ τὸν τῆς παροικίας ὑμῶν χρόνον ἀναστράφητε· εἰδότες ὅτι οὐ φθαρτοῖς, ἀργυρίῳ ἢ χρυσίῳ, ἐλυτρώθητε ἐκ τῆς ματαίας ὑμῶν ἀναστροφῆς πατροπαραδότου, ἀλλὰ τιμίῳ αἵματι ὡς ἀμνοῦ ἀμώμου καὶ ἀσπίλου Χριστοῦ, προεγνωσμένου μὲν πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου, φανερωθέντος δὲ ἐπ’ ἐσχάτου τῶν χρόνων δι’ ὑμᾶς τοὺς δι’ αὐτοῦ πιστοὺς εἰς θεὸν τὸν ἐγείραντα αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν καὶ δόξαν αὐτῷ δόντα, ὥστε τὴν πίστιν ὑμῶν καὶ ἐλπίδα εἶναι εἰς θεόν.

records.literal_gloss: And if [as] Father you call on the [one] impartially judging according to the of each work, in fear the of the sojourning of you time conduct yourselves, \v 18 knowing that not with perishable [things], silver or gold, you were ransomed from the futile of you way of life handed down from fathers, \v 19 but with precious blood as of a lamb unblemished and spotless, of Christ, \v 20 foreknown on one hand before [the] foundation of [the] world, made manifest on the other hand at [the] last of the times for the sake of you, \v 21 the [ones] through him believing into God, the [one] having raised him out of dead [ones] and glory to him having given, so that the faith of you and hope to be in God.

en.L: And if you call on as Father the one who judges without partiality according to each [one's] work, conduct yourselves in fear during the time of your stay as foreigners, \v 18 knowing that not with perishable [things], silver or gold, were you ransomed from your futile way of life handed down from [your] fathers, \v 19 but with precious blood, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot, [the blood] of {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, \v 20 foreknown before [the] foundation of [the] world but made visible at [the] last of the times for your sake, \v 21 who through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} [are] believing in God, the one who raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} out of [the] dead and gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} glory, so that your faith and hope [would] be in God.
en.B: If you call on God as Father, the one who judges each person by what they have done and shows no favoritism, then live in fear of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for as long as you are strangers far from home. \v 18 For you know the price of your release from the useless way of living you inherited from your forefathers. That price was not silver or gold, things that decay, \v 19 but the precious blood of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, who was like a lamb without flaw or stain. \v 20 God knew {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} before the world was made, and in this final age {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} known for your sake. \v 21 It is through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} that you trust in God, who raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from the dead and gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} glory. So your faith and hope are fixed on God.
en.R: You pray to God as your Father. But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} judges everyone fairly by what they have done, without taking sides. So while you live here as people far from home, live in awe of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 18 You know that you were set free from the empty way of life your ancestors handed down to you. The price was not paid with silver or gold, which do not last. \v 19 It was paid with the precious blood of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. He was like a perfect lamb, with no flaw or spot. \v 20 God had chosen {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for this before the world was made. Now, in these last days, {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} has appeared for your sake. \v 21 Because of what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done, you trust in God. God raised {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} from the dead and gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} glory. So now your faith and hope are in God.

decisions.choice: verses 17-21 are one record: verse 18 continues the sentence of verse 17
alternatives: two records, split at the raised dot after verse 17
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT puts a raised dot after ἀναστράφητε, but εἰδότες ("knowing") in verse 18 has no verb of its own outside the clause it introduces; it gives the reason for the command "conduct yourselves in fear". The clause cannot stand alone, so the two belong to one sentence.

decisions.choice: "if" of a real condition: since you do call on God as Father
decisions.reason: The readers do pray to God as Father (1:2-3). εἰ here states a fact and draws a consequence: the Father they pray to is also the impartial judge.

decisions.choice: God judges each person by what they have done, without favoring anyone
decisions.reason: ἀπροσωπολήμπτως is "without receiving faces", a Hebrew idiom for partiality (Deuteronomy 10:17; Acts 10:34; Romans 2:11). ἔργον is singular: each one's work taken as a whole.

decisions.choice: fear: reverent awe toward God as judge
decisions.reason: The fear is directed at the Father who judges. Peter elsewhere tells the readers not to fear people (3:6, 14) but to fear God (2:17).

decisions.choice: the time of living as foreigners: life now, away from their true home
decisions.reason: παροικίας is the life of a resident foreigner, the same idea as 1:1 and 2:11. The Greek Bible uses it of Israel in Egypt (Acts 13:17).

decisions.choice: ransomed: set free by the payment of a price
alternatives: delivered, with no thought of a price
decisions.reason: ἐλυτρώθητε is from the verb used of buying freedom for a slave or captive. The contrast with silver and gold makes the idea of a price clear. Isaiah 52:3 has the LORD telling his people "you will be redeemed without money"; Mark 10:45 speaks of Jesus' life as a ransom.

decisions.choice: an empty way of life handed down from their ancestors
decisions.reason: ματαίας is used in the Greek Bible of idols and the life built around them (Acts 14:15). πατροπαραδότου is "handed down from fathers". Together they point to the traditional religion of non-Jewish readers (compare 4:3).

decisions.choice: Christ is the lamb without defect offered to God, recalling the Passover lamb
decisions.reason: The Passover lamb had to be without defect (Exodus 12:5), as did every sacrifice (Leviticus 22:20). Coming after the language of ransom from bondage, the picture recalls Israel's rescue from Egypt; Isaiah 53:7 compares the suffering servant to a lamb.

decisions.choice: God knew Christ beforehand, before creation, and has now made him visible in the last times
decisions.reason: προεγνωσμένου uses the same root as "foreknowledge" in 1:2: God's knowing and choosing in advance. φανερωθέντος speaks of his appearing in history. μέν and δέ set the two times side by side: before the world, and at the end of the times.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "believing" as an adjective
alternatives: "believing" as a participle of the verb
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts have the participle of the verb "believe" in place of the adjective πιστοὺς. The meaning is the same. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: result: so that your faith and your hope are in God
alternatives: so that your faith is also hope in God
decisions.reason: ὥστε gives the result of God's raising and glorifying Christ. The two nouns can be taken together as the subject ("your faith and hope are in God") or "hope" can be the predicate ("your faith is also hope"). The first is the simpler reading.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L), {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R); {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} for God and for Christ
decisions.reason: Title and pronoun settings.

decisions.choice: in fear of him
decisions.reason: Balanced says whom the fear is directed to, following meaning decision m4.

decisions.choice: live in awe of him
decisions.reason: In plain English "fear" alone sounds like terror. Readable says it is the awe owed to God.

decisions.choice: the price of your release; the price was paid
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the idea of a ransom price explicit (meaning decision m6).

decisions.choice: God had chosen him for this; Because of what he has done
decisions.reason: Readable explains foreknowledge as God's choosing beforehand (as 1:2), and "through him" as what Christ has done.

decisions.choice: your stay as foreigners (L); strangers far from home (B); people far from home (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:1, the words say what the readers' position is without suggesting they were driven out.

source.text: Τὰς ψυχὰς ὑμῶν ἡγνικότες ἐν τῇ ὑπακοῇ τῆς ἀληθείας εἰς φιλαδελφίαν ἀνυπόκριτον ἐκ καρδίας ἀλλήλους ἀγαπήσατε ἐκτενῶς, ἀναγεγεννημένοι οὐκ ἐκ σπορᾶς φθαρτῆς ἀλλὰ ἀφθάρτου, διὰ λόγου ζῶντος θεοῦ καὶ μένοντος·

records.literal_gloss: The souls of you having purified in the obedience of the truth unto brotherly love unhypocritical, from heart one another love earnestly, \v 23 having been begotten again not of seed perishable but imperishable, through word living of God and remaining.

en.L: Having purified your souls by obedience to the truth for unpretended {{gender:love of brothers and sisters|brotherly love}}, love one another from [the] heart, intensely, \v 23 having been begotten again not from perishable seed but [from] imperishable, through [the] word of God, living and remaining.
en.B: Now that you have made yourselves pure by obeying the truth, so that you have a genuine love for your {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, keep loving one another from the heart with all your strength. \v 23 You have been born anew, not from a seed that dies but from one that cannot die, through the word of God, which is alive and lasts.
en.R: You obeyed the truth, and that has made you pure, so that now you can truly love each other as {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}. So love each other with all your heart, and keep on doing it. \v 23 For you have been born again. This new life did not come from a seed that dies. It came from a seed that can never die: the word of God, which is alive and lasts.

decisions.choice: the readers purified themselves when they obeyed the truth, and they remain purified
decisions.reason: ἡγνικότες is active and perfect: they purified their own selves, and the result lasts. They did it by obeying the truth, that is, by accepting the gospel, perhaps with baptism in view (compare 3:21). ψυχὰς again means their whole selves (1:9).

decisions.choice: the truth: the message of the gospel
decisions.reason: Obeying "the truth" is accepting God's message about Jesus Christ, which 1:25 calls the word announced to them.

decisions.choice: sincere love for fellow believers as family
decisions.reason: φιλαδελφίαν is love among brothers and sisters, used in the New Testament for love among believers (Romans 12:10; 1 Thessalonians 4:9). ἀνυπόκριτον means without play-acting: real love, not a show.

decisions.choice: earnestly: with full effort, intensely and without letting up
decisions.reason: ἐκτενῶς comes from the idea of stretching out. Peter uses the adjective for love again in 4:8.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: no "through the Spirit", no "pure" before "heart", and no "forever" after "remaining"
alternatives: "obedience to the truth through the Spirit"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "through the Spirit" after "truth" and "forever" at the end of verse 23 (from verse 25). Some important early manuscripts read "from a pure heart". The SBLGNT has the shorter text in each place; none changes the main meaning. Reviewers must check these against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: living and remaining describe the word of God
alternatives: they describe God: "the word of the living and remaining God"
decisions.reason: The two participles can go with "word" or with "God". The quotation that follows says "the word of the Lord remains forever" (1:25), so it is the word that remains, and it is living because it gives new birth.

decisions.choice: seed: the source of the new life, as seed is the source of birth
decisions.reason: σπορᾶς continues the image of new birth from 1:3. Natural life comes from seed that dies; this life comes from God's word, which does not.

decisions.choice: {{gender:love of brothers and sisters|brotherly love}} (L); {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: The love is for every believer, women and men. The traditional wording stays available as the alternative.

decisions.choice: with all your strength (B); with all your heart, and keep on doing it (R)
decisions.reason: Following meaning decision m4: the word says how hard and how constantly they are to love.

decisions.choice: You obeyed the truth, and that has made you pure
alternatives: Having purified your souls by obedience to the truth
decisions.reason: Readable turns the participle into its own sentence, telling first what the readers did.

source.text: διότι πᾶσα σὰρξ ὡς χόρτος, καὶ πᾶσα δόξα αὐτῆς ὡς ἄνθος χόρτου· ἐξηράνθη ὁ χόρτος, καὶ τὸ ἄνθος ἐξέπεσεν·

records.literal_gloss: because all flesh [is] like grass, and all [the] glory of it like [the] flower of grass; withered the grass, and the flower fell off;

en.L: For "all flesh [is] like grass, and all its glory like [the] flower of grass; the grass withered, and the flower fell off;
en.B: For "all people are like grass, and all their glory is like a wildflower. The grass dries up and the flower drops off.
en.R: As Scripture says, "People are like grass, and all their glory is like a flower in a field. The grass dries up, and the flower falls off.

decisions.choice: verses 24-25 quote Isaiah 40:6-8
decisions.reason: Isaiah 40 opens God's message of comfort to his people in exile, people far from home like Peter's readers. Peter follows the Greek of Isaiah closely. Where the Greek has "glory", the Hebrew has a word for loyal love or faithfulness: human loyalty fades like a flower. The quotation is not introduced with a formula; διότι links it to verse 23 as the reason the word of God is said to remain.

decisions.choice: flesh: human beings in their weakness and mortality
alternatives: the body as opposed to the spirit
decisions.reason: "All flesh" is a Hebrew way of saying all humankind (Genesis 6:12; Isaiah 40:5), here with the stress on how short human life is.

decisions.choice: a general truth: what always happens to grass and flowers
alternatives: a single event in the past
decisions.reason: ἐξηράνθη and ἐξέπεσεν are past tense in form but state what always happens, as proverbs do.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "all its glory", and "like grass"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "all the glory of man" in place of "its glory". Some manuscripts lack "like" before "grass", as the Greek of Isaiah does. The meaning is not changed. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: all people (B); People (R)
decisions.reason: Following meaning decision m2: "flesh" in current English means the body; the phrase means all humankind.

decisions.choice: As Scripture says
decisions.reason: Readable tells the reader that a quotation begins.

decisions.choice: dries up, drops off (present tense)
decisions.reason: English states a general truth in the present tense (meaning decision m3). Literal keeps the past tense of the Greek.

source.text: τὸ δὲ ῥῆμα κυρίου μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.

records.literal_gloss: but the word of [the] Lord remains into the age.

en.L: But the word of [the] Lord remains forever."
en.B: But the word of the Lord lasts forever."
en.R: But the word of the Lord lasts forever."

decisions.choice: the end of the quotation of Isaiah 40:8; the Lord here stands for God, whose name is in the Hebrew
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 40:8 the Hebrew reads "the word of our God will stand forever", and the Greek of Isaiah has "the word of our God". Peter has κυρίου, "Lord", the Greek Bible's usual word for God's own name, the LORD. Since the next sentence says this word is the good news about Jesus, the title may also point to Jesus as Lord.

decisions.choice: forever
decisions.reason: εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, "into the age", is the ordinary Greek expression for "forever".

decisions.choice: the word: God's spoken message, which remains
decisions.reason: ῥῆμα is a spoken word or message, nearly the same as λόγου in 1:23. μένει repeats the participle "remaining" of 1:23: God's word lasts when everything human fades.

decisions.choice: Lord
decisions.reason: The Greek has "Lord", not God's name, so English writes "Lord"; meaning decision m1 says what stands in Isaiah.

decisions.choice: lasts
decisions.reason: The same English word as "lasts" in 1:23, so the reader can see that Peter repeats the verb.

source.text: τοῦτο δέ ἐστιν τὸ ῥῆμα τὸ εὐαγγελισθὲν εἰς ὑμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: and this is the word the having been proclaimed as good news to you.

en.L: And this is the word that was proclaimed as good news to you.
en.B: And that word is the good news that was announced to you.
en.R: And this word is the good news that was told to you.

decisions.choice: "this" is the word of the Lord just quoted: the lasting word of Isaiah is the gospel the readers heard
decisions.reason: τοῦτο points back to the word that remains forever. Peter identifies it with the message that brought the readers new birth (1:23).

decisions.choice: proclaimed as good news
decisions.reason: εὐαγγελισθὲν is the verb "to announce good news", the same as in 1:12.

decisions.choice: proclaimed as good news (L); the good news (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek has the verb, not the noun gospel, so all levels say "good news", as in 1:12.
